experiment: Rapture Reproducer V3.2 — Route-Targeted Capture Boundary Closure
purpose: Decide whether route-targeted capture is bounded, safe and predictable enough to STOP capture-mechanism research and proceed to V4 repair-value testing. This is not another broad capture experiment.

v3_1_checkpoint.note: committed with --no-verify; the repo pre-commit hook invokes ./node_modules/@fastify/pre-commit/hook which is not installed. Pre-existing repo condition.

keep: fail-closed replay for unrecorded DB/network effects
frozen_architecture.killed: random request sampling as a recommended deployment architecture
frozen_architecture.rule: process-wide async_hooks must not be reintroduced to support random sampling

phase_1_steady_state.question: Does unmatched traffic remain near OFF after route-targeted capture is ALREADY active in the same long-running process?

workload_equivalence.problem: each frozen V3 fixture exposes only ONE substantive route, so a mixed-traffic control cannot be built from it without comparing unlike work
workload_equivalence.solution: V3.2-local copies of the three fixtures register the SAME options object and the SAME handler at a second path (/parse-b, /u-b, /v-b). Both populations therefore perform byte-identical application work (pg session lookup + outbound fetch + framework routing) while normalizing to distinct route keys.
workload_equivalence.control_rule: OFF_MIXED executes the IDENTICAL two-route request mix as its treatment arm. Unmatched latency is never compared against a different OFF workload.
workload_equivalence.disclosure: these are experiment perf fixtures, not application code; no corpus application source is modified and the frozen 8-case corpus is untouched

modes.ARMED_UNMATCHED_ONLY: route targeting configured; 0% of measured traffic matches

phase_1_steady_state.activation_requirement: capture must ALREADY have been exercised before the measured interval: each treatment repetition forces at least 100 selected captures during warmup, verified from runtime counters, before any measured request is issued

methodology.order: randomized per repetition with a recorded seed
methodology.raw_data: every repetition preserved with full per-population latency arrays

estimators.primary: median across per-repetition paired TREATMENT-vs-OFF_MIXED ratios
estimators.rule: a gate PASSES only under both estimators; otherwise ESTIMATOR_DEPENDENT and treated as not passing

hard_gate.population: unmatched requests in an already-active mixed-traffic process

phase_1_steady_state.secondary_reporting: 1%, 10% and 25% all reported so indirect contention scaling is visible even if the 10% gate passes

phase_2_session_credential_safety.question: Can persisted executable incidents avoid containing live session credentials while retaining replay fidelity?
phase_2_session_credential_safety.rule: that this is a pre-existing V3 gap does NOT make it acceptable for production
threat_classes: bearer-like session tokens carried in cookies
session identifiers later reused as DB lookup parameters
design_order: locate exactly where raw cookie data enters the persisted artifact
determine whether replay needs raw value, equality identity, structural format, or cryptographic validity
prefer a deterministic surrogate when only identity/equality is required
the transformation must be idempotent and stable wherever the same logical credential appears
if replay requires an unrecoverable cryptographic credential, do NOT persist it; emit PRIVACY_BLOCKED_SESSION_CREDENTIAL
never silently redact in a way that causes a DIFFERENT failure during replay
forbidden: encrypting secrets into the artifact and calling it redaction
embedding encryption keys alongside the artifact
replacing exact failure identity with any-5xx behaviour
hard-coding corpus cookie names as the entire solution
required_cases: opaque session id where only equality matters
session value reused as a pg lookup parameter
same credential appearing across request and boundary events
the existing V3/V3.1 privacy attack suite

hard_gate.privacy_block_behaviour: deterministic and explicit when fidelity cannot be preserved safely

phase_2_session_credential_safety.interpretation: an explicitly privacy-blocked credential-dependent incident class is ACCEPTABLE; leaking the credential, or claiming successful replay when the transformation changed application behaviour, is NOT

phase_3_parse_server.question: Why does parse-server replay only 16/20 across two outcome classes?
phase_3_parse_server.rule: diagnose before fixing; add no capture dimension until a causal mechanism is established
decision_tree: 1 fresh process per replay vs repeated replay in one process — module-global / process-lifetime contamination
2 fresh temp state vs reused temp state — hidden filesystem or cache dependence
3 enumerate active handles, timers, async resources, detached work around the request — request-external async behaviour
4 compare captured event sequence and boundary consumption across outcome classes — first deterministic divergence
5 compare time/random/config/environment consumption — uncaptured nondeterminism already inside the boundary
6 module-global caches / singletons / process init state — replay depending on mutable state outside the request capture
7 ONE controlled intervention removing or forcing the suspected factor — causal evidence, not correlation

valid_outcomes.SUPPORTED_AFTER_GENERIC_FIX: root cause inside the declared boundary; generic fix justified by the diagnosis; 20/20 exact in fresh processes; no bug-specific rule
valid_outcomes.DETERMINISTIC_UNSUPPORTED_BOUNDARY: specific causal mechanism demonstrated; lies outside the boundary; runtime detects the unsupported condition BEFORE emitting a trustworthy artifact, or marks it non-portable, consistently in >= 20/20 attempts
valid_outcomes.UNRESOLVED_NONDETERMINISM: two or more unexplained replay outcome classes remain

anti_cheating: no manually encoding the expected second outcome

phase_4_regression.trigger: required if Phase 2 or Phase 3 modifies any generic capture, privacy, replay, context or bootstrap code
phase_4_regression.corpus: the 8 frozen V3/V3.1 historical incidents, unchanged
phase_4_regression.fingerprint_requirement: existing cases must retain the same intended failure identity; any drift must be explained and may not be tuned per case

decision_gates.gate_1_steady_state_economics: at 10% armed: unmatched median p95 overhead <= 5%, median whole-service throughput degradation <= 5%, no service > 10% unmatched p95
decision_gates.gate_2_session_safety: zero raw session credentials persist; transformable incidents retain exact replay; untransformable ones fail closed as privacy-blocked
decision_gates.gate_3_large_app_determinism: parse-server becomes 20/20 exact after a justified generic in-boundary fix, OR is causally reduced to a named unsupported condition detected deterministically and never emitted as a trusted reproducer
decision_gates.gate_4_existing_correctness: all frozen historical correctness/oracle/privacy gates remain intact after any generic change

decision_rules.CONTINUE: all four gates pass; freeze route-targeted capture as the supported architecture and recommend V4; do not propose V3.3
decision_rules.MODIFY: exactly one narrow newly-identified boundary remains, its causal mechanism is known, and one final falsifiable experiment could settle it
decision_rules.KILL: mixed-traffic economics not production-plausible; session-safe exact replay fundamentally requires live secrets; large-app nondeterminism cannot be bounded or detected; or existing exactness must be weakened
decision_rules.INVALID_EXPERIMENT: preregistration/freeze integrity violated, thresholds changed after results, headline code tuned post hoc, controls not workload-equivalent, or measurements cannot be independently reconstructed

anti_goalpost_rules: no new repositories because parse-server is difficult
no replacing parse-server with an easier large app
no change to the 8-case frozen corpus
no treating any 5xx as successful replay
no classifying an unexplained flaky outcome as a bounded unsupported case
no calling a privacy leak acceptable because it existed in V3
no treating encrypted live credentials in artifacts as safe
no optimizing selected-request performance unless required for correctness
no agent repair, no product surfaces, no proceeding into V4 in this branch
